title: 15tcu3u
Mu'awiya and Imam Ali: refusing allegiance, Siffin and the Arbitration
hook: While Imam Ali's right was plain, Mu'awiya did not pledge allegiance. At Siffin he fixed the Qur'an to spears.
scenes.0.text: In Damascus **Mu'awiya** had been maintaining an army for twenty years. **Umar** left him as governor of Syria. **Uthman** enlarged the province. The first appointment was not Uthman's. When **Imam Ali** became caliph he replaced governors for the sake of justice. He wanted to dismiss Mu'awiya from Syria as well. This was not about writing the faith inside him as a fact. It was for the sake of administration and justice. Mu'awiya refused both dismissal and allegiance. Allegiance is a pledge of loyalty. He did not give up his power before Imam Ali, the Prophet's wasi.
scenes.1.text: In the mosque of Damascus **Mu'awiya** showed the people the bloodied shirt of **Caliph Uthman**. He made his blood the pretext. The pretext was not justice but delaying allegiance. Where he said he demanded accountability, what he really wanted was the throne of Syria. While **Imam Ali**'s right was plain, he put the shirt forward and did not give allegiance.
scenes.2.text: **Imam Ali** wrote a letter to **Mu'awiya** in Syria and sent an envoy. First allegiance, then the court, he said. He asked that the reckoning for the blood be sought before the community was torn apart. Mu'awiya did not accept this. In 37 AH the two armies faced each other on the bank of the Euphrates, at **Siffin**. What was asked was allegiance first. The other side chose war.
scenes.3.text: At **Siffin** **Mu'awiya**'s men cut off the water of the Euphrates. When **Imam Ali** took the water he did not leave the Syrians without water. He gave water to his enemy. Later at Karbala the same wrong was committed. The water of the Prophet's descendant was cut off. Those who cut off the water at Siffin were the forerunners of this wrong.
scenes.4.text: At Siffin the elderly **Ammar b. Yasir** was martyred in **Imam Ali**'s ranks. The Prophet had foretold that a ==rebellious group== would kill him. A baghi is one who fights against the legitimate imam. That group was **Mu'awiya**'s army. When **Amr b. al-As** recalled the hadith, Mu'awiya twisted the saying: "Those who brought him killed him." The Prophet's report was clear. The other side turned this saying around in order to deny the report.
scenes.5.text: At Siffin, as the war turned in **Imam Ali**'s favor, at the proposal of **Amr b. al-As** pages of the Qur'an were fixed to spears. "Let the Book of God be arbiter between us," they said. This was not worship, it was ==a trick.== **Imam Ali** said it was a trick at that moment. A group in his army used the mushafs as a pretext and stopped him. The right was left half-finished when the Qur'an was hung on a spear.
scenes.6.text: At the arbitration meeting **Abu Musa** and **Amr b. al-As** sat down. In the widespread account, Abu Musa deposes Imam Ali as if taking off a ring, and Amr puts **Mu'awiya** at the head as if putting on a ring. The reliability of this account is disputed. The exact words vary by report. **Imam Ali** did not accept this result. The trick on the spear continued in this council too.
scenes.7.text: After the Arbitration **Imam Ali**'s ranks split. **Malik al-Ashtar** was Imam Ali's loyal commander. He is remembered as a front-rank man in battle and a trusted one in administration. Imam Ali sent him to the governorship of Egypt. It is reported that he was poisoned on the way. Wikipedia writes that this happened at Qulzum, through a bribed official and, in most accounts, with the poison mixed into honey. This is not a maqtal page. The description of the poison is not given. The same page also tells of those who rejoiced in Syria and of this saying of Mu'awiya: one of Imam Ali's two arms was cut off at Siffin with Ammar, the other now. **Mu'awiya** reached out to Egypt. The governor Muhammad b. Abi Bakr was killed. Busr b. Artat shed blood in the Hijaz and Yemen. The trick of the Arbitration continued with these attacks. **Imam Ali** was martyred in 40 AH, at a dawn prayer.
sunni.0.says: The Prophet's saying about Ammar, «a rebellious group will kill you».
sunni.1.says: The same hadith; the group that will kill Ammar.
sunni.2.says: Amr b. al-As reminding Mu'awiya of the hadith; the answer «those who brought him killed him».
sunni.3.says: The bank of the Euphrates, the raising of the mushafs, the Arbitration and the later events.
sunni.4.says: Tells of Siffin and the Arbitration in detail; also states that Imam Ali was closer to the right.
shia.0.says: A detailed account of Siffin; the seizing of the Euphrates and the tying of the mushafs to spears.
shia.1.says: Imam Ali's letters to Mu'awiya and his sermons on Siffin.
shia.2.says: Mu'awiya's stance toward Imam Ali and his role at Siffin.
disputes.0.title: y3yzlx
Why was allegiance not given?
disputes.0.sunni: That Mu'awiya did not give allegiance is told in both traditions. The Sunni majority understands his reason as the blood of Caliph Uthman, counts this as an error of ijtihad, and finds Imam Ali closer to the right.
disputes.0.shia: That Mu'awiya did not give allegiance is told in both traditions. In the Shia account the aim is power; Ammar's martyrdom also shows standing with Imam Ali.
disputes.1.title: mplnbw
Is there a trick in the Arbitration meeting?
disputes.1.sunni: The Arbitration meeting is told in both traditions. Amr's trick comes through the channel of Abu Mikhnaf, and many Sunni scholars look at the detail with caution.
disputes.1.shia: The Arbitration meeting is told in both traditions. In the Shia account Imam Ali was against this from the start and had said that the mushafs were a trick.
questions.0: Imam Ali said first order, then the case. What does this path make you think about protecting the blood of the community?
questions.1: Ammar was martyred in Imam Ali's ranks; the Prophet had foretold this. How does this report make you think about standing with the Ahl al-Bayt?
questions.2: When the mushafs were hung on spears, the war was left half-finished. What does this moment tell you about Imam Ali's patience and the community's later path?
summary: Mu'awiya refused allegiance. At Siffin Ammar was martyred beside Imam Ali. The mushafs were hung on spears and the Arbitration divided the army. Then Egypt was taken, Muhammad b. Abi Bakr was killed, and Malik al-Ashtar was poisoned on the road. Imam Ali was martyred in 40 AH.
key: The governor who did not give allegiance: Siffin, the mushafs and the Arbitration
notes.0: When Imam Ali dismissed him, Mu'awiya did not give up the governorship of Syria and did not give allegiance.
notes.1: He cited the blood of Caliph Uthman as the reason.
notes.2: At Siffin Ammar b. Yasir was martyred; the Prophet's hadith «a rebellious group will kill him» was recalled (Bukhari 447, Muslim 2915).
notes.3: As the war turned in Imam Ali's favor the mushafs were tied to spears and the Arbitration was accepted.
notes.4: Afterward Egypt was taken, Muhammad b. Abi Bakr was killed, and Malik al-Ashtar was poisoned on the road.
